AfterCardPlayed.maps_to: on_card_played (mummified_hand.py:22-29), dispatched by CombatState._resolve_card_play at combat.py:514
AfterCardPlayed.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and G3 per binding rule 4. The trigger matches (a Power play, MummifiedHand.cs:26-29) and the RNG stream matches (Rng.CombatCardSelection, MummifiedHand.cs:30, vs combat_rng.card_selection, mummified_hand.py:29), but the CANDIDATE SET does not: C# runs a four-tier fallback over two different cost predicates (MummifiedHand.cs:31-45) and the sim keeps a single `c.energy_cost > 0` filter with no fallback at all.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the sim's candidate filter reads the card's LOCAL cost; C# reads the cost WITH GLOBAL MODIFIERS (CostsEnergyOrStars(includeGlobalModifiers: true))
guards.issue: MECHANISM: MummifiedHand.cs:33 and :36 filter on `c.CostsEnergyOrStars(includeGlobalModifiers: true)`, which is `!EnergyCost.CostsX && EnergyCost.GetWithModifiers(CostModifiers.All) > 0` (CardModel.cs:1578-1592) -- the cost the player would actually pay right now, global modifiers included. mummified_hand.py:25 filters on `c.energy_cost`, which is the sim Card's own LOCAL cost (cards/base.py:222-232: free-this-turn, cost-this-turn, cost-this-combat and the per-turn delta) and nothing else; the sim's global cost modifiers live in the `modify_card_energy_cost` hook chain (hooks.py:196, consulted only at play time, combat.py:408) and the relic never asks it. So a card the player could already play for free still looks 'costing' to the sim and the free cost is spent on it. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py mummified-hand): CorruptionPower (powers.py:597) makes every SKILL cost 0 globally and is applied by the ported Ironclad Rare Power card cards/corruption.py:35. With Corruption up and a hand of [Inflame, Defend x4, Bash] the sim still reports energy_cost>0 for all four Defends (the probe prints the hook pricing them at 0) and freed a DEFEND; C#'s tier 1 admits only Bash, so the game frees the Bash. Both sides ported: Mummified Hand is Rare in the transcribed grab bag (relic_pools.py, executed by this module's `pool` probe). The mirror direction exists too: relic/spiked_gauntlets (spiked_gauntlets.py:26-31) RAISES Power costs, so a base-0 Power reads as costing in C#'s tier 2 and as free in the sim. Rule 7: CardModel.cs, powers.py, cards/base.py, hooks.py, combat.py, cards/corruption.py, relics/spiked_gauntlets.py and relic_pools.py are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE for RNG parity): C#'s tier-3 and tier-4 fallbacks do not exist in the sim, so when no hand card costs energy the sim picks nothing and skips the CombatCardSelection draw C# takes
guards.issue: MECHANISM: MummifiedHand.cs:38-45 keeps falling back -- `NextItem(list)` (base cost > 0, however cheap it is now) and finally `NextItem(cards)` (ANY hand card) -- so the game always picks a card when the hand is non-empty. mummified_hand.py:26-27 returns early instead. Rng.NextItem on an empty sequence takes no draw (Rng.cs:255-265), so C# consumes exactly ONE NextInt from the first non-empty tier; with a hand of nothing but 0-cost cards that is tier 4. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b10.py mummified-hand): after playing Inflame with [Dazed, Dazed] left in hand the sim consumes 0 card_selection draws and leaves both cards un-freed, where C# takes 1 draw and frees one. LIVE FOR RNG PARITY: the gameplay effect is nil (every candidate already costs 0, so SetToFreeThisTurn changes nothing), but combat_rng.card_selection is the run-level COMBAT_CARD_SELECTION stream in parity mode (combat_rng.py:21, rng.py:383), so the missing draw shifts every later card-selection roll for the rest of the run. Dormant for RL play -- the same live/dormant split relic/astrolabe N1 records. Reachable with no exotic content: Dazed is a ported 0-cost status generated by ported enemy powers, and any Ironclad Power card triggers the relic. Rule 7: Rng.cs, combat_rng.py, rng.py and relics/astrolabe.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: G3 (LIVE): AfterCardPlayed fires once per Replay iteration in C# and once per play in the sim, so a DOUBLED Power card frees two cards in the game and one in the sim
guards.issue: This is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G4 observed at this relic's own site -- CardModel.cs:1904-1965 builds a fresh CardPlay per iteration and fires Hook.AfterCardPlayed at :1959 INSIDE the loop, while combat.py:466 and :514 bracket the WHOLE play-count loop (combat.py:477-494). One verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3: G4 is a gap and is already labelled LIVE there, so this entry does not re-derive it. EXECUTED at this site (relic_probes_b10.py mummified-hand): with relic/throwing_axe (granted by the ported Tanx shrine, events/tanx.py) doubling the first play of the combat and Inflame as that first card, the sim frees ONE hand card where C# frees two -- and burns one CombatCardSelection draw instead of two. Rule 7: CardModel.cs, combat.py, relics/throwing_axe.py, events/tanx.py and the hook_dispatch seam record are not hashed here.

guards.rationale: Structurally satisfied: on_card_played is a combat hook dispatched only by a live CombatState, and C#'s own AfterCardPlayed dispatch is itself gated on IsInProgress (CardModel.cs:1957), so the relic's copy of the check is redundant on both sides. Checked deliberately rather than assumed, because combat.py:514 fires on_card_played BEFORE play_card's `_end_combat` call (combat.py:417-420), so a killing blow reaches this hook in the sim. It reaches it in C# too: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json G13 enumerates all six CheckWinCondition sites and none is inside CardModel.Play, so IsInProgress is still true when the game fires the hook. Rule 7: CardModel.cs, combat.py and the turn_structure record are unhashed here.

Multiplayer ownership plumbing: the sim has exactly one player and one hand (self.player.hand), so both the owner test and the per-owner pile lookup are structurally satisfied. Noted in the mapping rather than treated as a divergence, per PROMPT.md's scope note on multiplayer-only params.

guards.what: N3: X-cost cards are excluded from C#'s first three tiers -- is the sim's single filter equivalent for them?
guards.rationale: EXECUTED (relic_probes_b10.py mummified-hand). C# bars X-cost cards from tiers 1 and 2 via `!EnergyCost.CostsX` (CardModel.cs:1582, :1586) and from tier 3 because `GetWithModifiers(CostModifiers.None)` is 0 for them, so only tier 4 can ever pick one. The sim's three ported X-cost cards -- cascade, volley, whirlwind -- all set `_energy_cost = 0` alongside `energy_cost_x = True` (cards/whirlwind.py:29, :33), so `c.energy_cost > 0` excludes them as well. The tier-4 asymmetry is G2's subject, not a separate defect. Rule 7: CardModel.cs and cards/whirlwind.py are unhashed here.
